catalog.container_strategy: Build from the verified official release archive in an independent directory; install into a resource-local prefix, retain source/license, and use command-local runtime libraries. Keep existing system packages and versions separate.
catalog.purpose: The hwloc 2.14 stable CPU/NUMA/cache/LinuxIO core profile, with XML replay and C API; independent of APT hwloc.
qualification_gaps: Native Linux x86_64 source build and bounded functional checks passed on the recorded host. Exact APT-image deployment and physical target qualification remain separate.
catalog.size_basis: Complete official release archive measured locally and matched to the published SHA-256; logical source bytes sum regular TAR members.

notes: This explicitly named core profile includes Linux CPU/NUMA/cache discovery, LinuxIO, synthetic topologies and the built-in XML backend. GUI/Cairo, PCI/libpciaccess, libudev, GPU/OpenCL/CUDA/NVML/RSMI/LevelZero/GL plugins and libxml2 are disabled.
Existing APT hwloc 2.10.0 remains available at its system path with its own build features. This package does not remove or replace it.
Discovery support and allowed CPU sets describe the process-visible container namespace. A successful XML/API check does not prove that a later CPU or memory binding request is allowed.
No deployment check changes parent affinity, memory policy, kernel parameters, governors or device permissions.
Each installed ELF tool uses a package-local launcher to load its own shared library. The launcher does not alter the parent environment.
A prebuilt package must record architecture, libc, compiler and build profile. Native build evidence is not an OCI image or arbitrary-platform qualification.
pkg-config metadata uses its containing prefix; legacy libtool .la files retain build-prefix metadata and are not advertised as relocatable link inputs.

notes: This profile includes CPU/NUMA/cache discovery, LinuxIO with native Linux sysfs PCI discovery, synthetic topologies and the built-in XML backend. External libpciaccess probing is explicitly disabled through the upstream configure header-cache setting; GUI/Cairo, libudev, GPU/OpenCL/CUDA/NVML/RSMI/LevelZero/GL plugins and libxml2 remain disabled.
Existing APT hwloc 2.10.0 remains available at its system path with its own build features. This package does not remove or replace it.
Discovery support and allowed CPU sets describe the process-visible container namespace. A successful XML/API check does not prove that a later CPU or memory binding request is allowed.
No deployment check changes parent affinity, memory policy, kernel parameters, governors or device permissions.
Each installed ELF tool uses a package-local launcher to load its own shared library. The launcher does not alter the parent environment.
A prebuilt package must record architecture, libc, compiler and build profile. Native build evidence is not an OCI image or arbitrary-platform qualification.
pkg-config metadata uses its containing prefix; legacy libtool .la files retain build-prefix metadata and are not advertised as relocatable link inputs.

Build 2 additionally qualifies fresh shared/static consumers and verifies that the dynamic API probe resolves the library in this exact prefix. Hardware counters, MSR access and frequency measurement are not enabled by these checks.

Linux sysfs PCI discovery is independent of the optional libpciaccess backend. The original --disable-pci core profile is retained with its original definition/recipe in the complete workspace baseline; build 2 restores the built-in Linux discovery path without adding an external runtime dependency.
usage.summary: The hwloc 2.14 CPU/NUMA/cache/LinuxIO profile, including native Linux sysfs PCI discovery, XML replay and C API.
